# mapuce.data.2020

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/AcidyBee/mapuce.data.2020/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/AcidyBee/mapuce.data.2020/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of `mapuce.data.2020` is to provide ready-to-use datasets for MAPUCE models, derived from the 2020 French census (RP INDCVI) and the 2022 administrative boundaries.

## Installation

You can install the development version of mapuce.data.2020 like so:

``` r
remotes::install_github("AcidyBee/mapuce.data.2020")
```

## Source

Raw data come from the INSEE RP INDCVI 2020 detail files and the 2022 administrative boundaries. See `data-raw/DATASET.R` and `data-raw/_targets.R` for the generation pipeline.

## Datasets

| Dataset | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `mapuce_indcvi` | Semantic data for France (RP 2020) |
| `mapuce_indcvi_za` | Semantic data restricted to Île-de-France |
| `lut_iris_atome_indcvi` | Lookup table between IRIS and `atome_indcvi` |
| `spatial_iris` | Spatial data at IRIS level (2022 boundaries, WGS84) | 
| `spatial_atome_indcvi` | Spatial data at `atome_indcvi` level (2022 boundaries, WGS84) |
| `*_za` variants | Same datasets restricted to Île-de-France |

## Data File Naming Convention

Files follow `{dataset}_{zone}.rda` format:
- `spatial_iris_za.rda`: zone A corresponds to Île-de-France
- `mapuce_indcvi.rda`: no zone defined means the whole country

## Data Compression and Size  

This package contains large datasets compressed with `xz`, except for `mapuce_indcvi` which is compressed with `bzip2` (optimal compression).  
- Total installed size: ~160 MB  
- Primary use: high-resolution spatial data for France, at IRIS and `atome_indcvi` granularity  
- To reduce local disk usage, load only needed datasets with `data("dataset_name", package = "mapuce.data.2020")`.

| Dataset | Size |
| :--- | :--- |
| `mapuce_indcvi` | ~50 MB |
| `mapuce_indcvi_za` | ~10 MB |
| `lut_iris_atome_indcvi` | ~70 KB |
| `lut_iris_atome_indcvi_za` | ~10 KB |
| `spatial_iris` | ~60 MB | 
| `spatial_atome_indcvi` | ~20 MB |
| `spatial_iris_za` | ~3 MB | 
| `spatial_atome_indcvi_za` | ~2 MB |

## Example

Data for this project are aggregated at what Insee calls cantville granularity: it corresponds to:
- IRIS for dense areas
- COMMUNE or CANTON for lesser population areas

The atome_indcvi key has been created to link semantic and spatial information for Insee RP indcvi detail files. The atome_indcvi variable is the smallest possible entity for indcvi files, and is obtained using hierarchically (IRIS < COMMUNE < CANTON) the information available for each observation in the file.

### Semantic data

Head of semantic data for zone A: Ile de France. The rows correspond to the city of Paris.

You can see that for the 6 first rows of the dataset, the 9 digits iris_code is available. On the other hand, for Paris the cv_code (cantville) is not complete: it corresponds to the DEPARTEMENT granularity. It is replaced with arm_code which only exists for the 3 major french cities: Lyon, Marseille and Paris).

```{r}
data("mapuce_indcvi_za", package = "mapuce.data.2020")
head(mapuce_indcvi_za)
```

### Spatial data

Corresponding choropleth map data for zone A (Ile de France)

```{r}
data("spatial_iris", package = "mapuce.data.2020")
data("spatial_atome_indcvi_za", package = "mapuce.data.2020")
spatial_atome_indcvi_za %>% 
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(fill = .data$atome_indcvi_type)) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf() +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = spatial_iris %>% dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(.data$iris_code, "^75")), 
                   linetype = "dotted", linewidth = .15, fill = NA, color = "white") +
  ggplot2::coord_sf() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "atome_indcvi and IRIS boundaries in Île-de-France") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

...and a zoom for Paris

```{r}
data("spatial_iris", package = "mapuce.data.2020")
data("spatial_atome_indcvi_za", package = "mapuce.data.2020")
spatial_atome_indcvi_za %>% 
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(.data$atome_indcvi, "^75")) %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(fill = .data$atome_indcvi_type)) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf() +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = spatial_iris %>%   dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(.data$iris_code, "^75")), 
                   linetype = "dotted", linewidth = .15, fill = NA, color = "white") +
  ggplot2::coord_sf() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "atome_indcvi and IRIS boundaries in Île-de-France") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```
